$comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): the C99 6.7.4p7 INLINE DEFINITION -- every file-scope declaration of `pick` in cu_a.c spells `inline` without `extern`, so that definition 'does not provide an external definition for the function' and cu_a emits NO body for it. ★ THE EXIT CODE NAMES WHICH BODY RAN. The two bodies return DIFFERENT values (7 in cu_a, 42 in cu_b), so exit 42 can only mean cu_b's external definition executed -- which can only happen if cu_a emitted nothing. This is the strongest OBSERVABLE form of 'the symbol is absent from this TU's image': a symbol dump would assert the same fact without proving the program still behaves. RED-ON-DISABLE, two ways, both loud: emit cu_a's body and the link fails K_SymbolRedefinedAcrossUnits (two external definitions); suppress it without leaving the ExternFunction declaration behind and the reference has nothing to bind to. MEASURED: `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0 -c cu_a.c` + `nm` shows `_pick` UNDEFINED (not defined-and-weak), and the clang-linked pair independently exits 42.
